segments.t: Outside the radio building, an angry crowd of conservative demonstrators gathers to protest against Sacha Hartman's movie. Learning that Mathias and Isabelle are on their way, Camille coordinates with Andrea to hurry the director into a waiting cab. Listen to the scene in French first.
Non, Camille. Vous faites erreur.
Mathias vient ici avec Isabelle Adjani.
Je dois trouver un moyen d'éloigner Hartman.
Donne-moi les clés de la voiture.
Tu es sûre de vouloir conduire?
Regarde dehors! C'est quoi ça?
C'est une manifestation anti-Hartman.
Ils ne sont pas très accueillants.
Ils cherchent la bagarre.
Camille? Des militants sont devant le studio.
Si Sacha les voit, ça va dégénérer.
Bon, sors par derrière avec lui.
Je t'envoie un taxi tout de suite.
Merci beaucoup, Camille!
Je monte dans ce taxi.
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
Non, Camille. Vous faites erreur.
'No, Camille. You are mistaken.' Camille corrects Mathias on the surprise phone call. The verbal idiom faire erreur polite defers identity confusion.
Mathias vient ici avec Isabelle Adjani.
'Mathias is coming here with Isabelle Adjani.' She realizes an ambush is underway. The present tense of venir expresses immediate imminent arrival.
Je dois trouver un moyen d'éloigner Hartman.
'I must find a way to get Hartman away.' Camille plans rapid evasive action. The semi-auxiliary devoir governs an infinitive phrase of necessity.
Donne-moi les clés de la voiture.
'Give me the car keys.' Sacha impatiently asks for their vehicle. The imperative combines the verb donner with attached object pronoun.
Tu es sûre de vouloir conduire?
'Are you sure you want to drive?' Camille hesitates to hand over vehicle control. The adjective follows the second-person singular copula.
Regarde dehors! C'est quoi ça?
'Look outside! What is that?' Sacha spots commotion on the street below. The colloquial interrogative c'est quoi questions visual phenomena.
C'est une manifestation anti-Hartman.
'It is an anti-Hartman demonstration.' Camille identifies the hostile crowd. The compound prefix attaches directly to the director name.
Ils ne sont pas très accueillants.
'They are not very welcoming.' Sacha dryly observes the vocal protesters. The negative frame modifies the plural descriptive adjective.
Ils cherchent la bagarre.
'They are looking for a fight.' Camille warns of imminent danger outside. The verbal phrase signifies seeking physical confrontation.
Camille? Des militants sont devant le studio.
'Camille? Activists are in front of the studio.' Andrea calls with alarming updates. The spatial preposition locates the demonstrators relative to the entrance.
Si Sacha les voit, ça va dégénérer.
'If Sacha sees them, things will escalate.' Andrea fears an explosive public scene. The conditional clause predicts uncontrolled escalation.
Bon, sors par derrière avec lui.
'Right, sneak out the back with him.' Andrea gives clear tactical escape directions. The imperative of sortir specifies an emergency rear exit.
Je t'envoie un taxi tout de suite.
'I am sending you a taxi right now.' Camille arranges a swift getaway car. The temporal phrase emphasizes rapid transport coordination.
Merci beaucoup, Camille!
'Thank you very much, Camille!' Sacha expresses heartfelt relief at her quick thinking. The polite expression conveys heartfelt gratitude.
Je monte dans ce taxi.

'I am getting into this taxi.' The director safely steps into the vehicle. The prepositional verb signifies boarding the vehicle. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.

Je monte dans ce taxi.
Thanks to Camille's quick reflexes and Andrea's warning, Sacha slips safely into a taxi before Mathias and Isabelle arrive. Listen to the French scene once more.
Mission accomplie, Andréa.
